prerequisites: Knowledge of the fundamentals of Chemistry is highly recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic knowledge about the nature, classification and properties of ferrous materials, including cast irons. These contents are part of the body of knowledge and operational capabilities in the specific fields of mechanical engineering, with regard to the choice of materials in the design process, and in the management of production technologies and industrial plants.
Recognize the fundamental properties of the various classes of steel, cast iron, or aluminum alloy.
Identify, starting from the structural demands that the design places on the material, the steel, cast iron or aluminum alloy most suitable for a given application, and the related supply status.
Analyze and manage the various phases of the component production process mechanical taking into account the properties of the metallic material involved.
Develop independent judgment and learning ability by performing simple problem-solving exercises.

Acquire knowledge on the nature, classification and properties of ferrous metals, with hints on the same issues for aluminium alloys. These subjects constitute a fundamental part of the wealth of knowledge at the basis of mechanical engineering in the fields of mechanical design and materials processing.
Identify the main properties of the different groups of steels, cast irons and aluminium alloys.
Select the best steel, cast iron or aluminium alloy, and the corresponding initial state, on the bases of the design functional requirements.
Correctly analyze and govern the production stages of mechanical components, taking into account the final properties of the used material.
Improve autonomy, and communication, learning and critical skills through simple exercises.

syllabus_topics: Notes on the crystalline structure of metals
State diagrams (complete miscibility, eutectic, peritectic) and their reading
Special steels (reclamation, self-hardening, carburizing, nitriding, bearing; rope, surface hardening)
Exercises on Status diagrams, CCT and TTT diagrams, steel recognition and estimation of their mechanical properties
Laboratory activities: Guided tours for student groups
Deformation of metals and strengthening methods in metals
Steels: primary steel production (blast furnace, converter), scrap and recycling (electrical furnaces)
Steels for general use, alloy steels, tool steels, stainless steels
Exercises: Phase diagrams, TTT and CCT curves, Steel classification and calculation of their mechanical properties
Visits in the lab, sample preparation, optical microscopy, hardness
assessment_rules: The exam consists of an oral exam with questions relating to all topics. The oral exam will be divided into 3 questions, each evaluated with a score between 0 and 10 points. The first question will always concern CCT curves, Fe-C state diagram, remediation treatment, or traction curves. If the student does not fully answer the first question, the exam is considered concluded and failed. The grading scheme is based on a scale of 30 points, with successful completion leading to grades from 18 to 30.
